title: How to Create a Retirement Income Plan With Multiple Accounts
description: Sequencing withdrawals from 401(k), IRA, Roth, and Taxable accounts.
content:
Accumulating wealth is simple: save and invest. Decumulating wealth is complex. You have different buckets—Pre-Tax (401k), Tax-Free (Roth), and Taxable (Brokerage)—each with different tax rules. If you pull money from the wrong account at the wrong time, you can trigger a tax bomb, higher Medicare premiums, or lost compounding. This guide explains the 'Withdrawal Sequencing' strategy to stretch your portfolio longevity by 5-10 years.

Key Takeaways

  • Conventional Wisdom (Sequential): Sell Taxable assets first, then Traditional, then Roth. This lets the tax-advantaged money grow the longest. This is the standard advice.
  • Modern Wisdom (Proportional): Withdraw from all three buckets annually to manage your tax bracket. 'Fill up' the 12% tax bracket with Traditional withdrawals, then top off with Roth/Cash.
  • RMD Defense: If you save Traditional for last, you will have massive Required Minimum Distributions at age 73, pushing you into a high tax bracket. Spend Traditional early to flatten the tax curve.
  • Roth as the 'Swing' Voter: Use Roth withdrawals for big, lumpy expenses (new car, big trip) to avoid spiking your taxable income for that year.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Your 'Adjusted Gross Income' (AGI) determines more than just taxes. It determines your Medicare Part B premiums (IRMAA) and the taxability of your Social Security. Keeping AGI low by using Roth/Cash strategically saves you thousands in hidden surcharges.

The Account Roles

Assign a job to each bucket.

1. Taxable Brokerage (First Out)

Tax Rate: Capital Gains (0-15%).
Role: The Bridge. Spend this first to let IRAs grow.
Bonus: Sell 'Losers' to offset gains (Tax Loss Harvesting) to generate tax-free cash.

2. Traditional IRA / 401(k) (The Base)

Tax Rate: Ordinary Income (10-37%).
Role: The Salary. Withdraw enough to fill the standard deduction ($29k) and the lowest brackets. Do not withdraw more than necessary.

3. Roth IRA (Last Out)

Tax Rate: 0%.
Role: The Legacy / Emergency. Since it has no RMDs and grows tax-free, let it compound as long as possible. Pass it to heirs tax-free.

Tactical Sequencing

  1. The 'Gap Year' Conversion: Between retirement (e.g., 60) and Social Security (e.g., 70), your income is low. Don't just spend cash. deliberately withdraw/convert Traditional IRA money to fill the 12% bracket. Pay low taxes now to avoid high RMD taxes later.
  2. Specific ID Selling: In your taxable account, sell shares with the highest cost basis first. This generates the least amount of taxable gain.
  3. Dividend Sweep: Stop reinvesting dividends in retirement. Have them sweep to your checking account. This acts as a natural paycheck without requiring you to sell shares.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need software?

Yes. Optimizing this manually is hard. Tools like NewRetirement or a CPA can model your multi-year tax liability. A 1% efficiency gain here is worth huge money.

What about the HSA?

Save it for last. It can pay Medicare premiums tax-free. Or, use it to pay for Long Term Care late in life.

Can I spend dividends from my IRA?

Yes, but the IRS treats it as a withdrawal. It is taxed as income, not as a favorable dividend rate. Inside an IRA, a dividend is just cash.
